title: Reading a room by its furniture
target: How to use the furniture in an R.E.P.O. room as information, given that chairs, tables and lamps are named per room, that a furnished room can hold a screen, and that even a fish is filed as a valuable.
prerequisites: A torch and enough battery to keep it on
One hand free for the cart
A crew that will not wander off in the dark

steps.do: Work out which room you are in from its furniture before you start loading the cart.
steps.because: tables are named by room and by size, an arctic round table and a small arctic one among them (Arctic Round Table, Arctic Small Table)

steps.do: Use the big pieces as landmarks when the lights are out.
steps.because: chairs are named in kinds, an armchair, a plain chair, a big chair and a camp chair among them (Armchair, Chair, Chair Big, Camp Chair)

steps.do: Let the lamps tell you which rooms are worth searching.
steps.because: lamps are named for the rooms, a small arctic ceiling lamp among them (Arctic Ceiling Lamp Small, Arctic Celing Lamp Small)

steps.do: Check the screen in a furnished room instead of walking past it.
steps.because: a furnished room can hold a flat-screen television of its own (Flat screen TV, FlatScreenTV)

steps.do: Do not write a fish off as decoration: on this site it is filed as a valuable.
steps.because: fish are named as a valuable of their own, with a mesh and a material beside them and a museum version (Fish valuable, Valuable Fish, Valuable Museum Fish, FishMesh, FishMaterial)

commonMistakes: Reading a room by its loot while the furniture has already told you which theme it is.
Walking into a dark room without noting the landmarks you will need on the way back.
Leaving a fish behind because it looked like scenery.
Packing the cart before you know which part of the level you are standing in.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
